items.title: Four Dilemmas Aimed at the Sovereign Creator

items.zh: 今當問彼：汝何所欲？嗢拕南曰：功能無體性，攝、不攝相違，有用、及無用，為因，成過失。自在天等變化功能，為用業方便為因？為無因耶？若用業方便為因者，唯此功能用業方便為因，非餘世間，不應道理。若無因者，唯此功能無因而有，非世間物，不應道理。
items.en: One should now question them. A summary verse states: function has no substance; inclusion and exclusion both contradict; usefulness and uselessness; and as cause, every option fails. What do you actually intend: does the sovereign lord's transformative power have, as its cause, deliberate effort and method, or does it have no cause at all? If it has deliberate effort and method as its cause, then insisting only this power operates this way, while nothing else in the world does, makes no sense. If it has no cause at all, then insisting only this power exists uncaused, while nothing else in the world does, makes no sense either.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？此大自在為墮世間攝？為不攝耶？若言攝者，此大自在則同世法，而能遍生世間，不應道理。若不攝者，則是解脫，而言能生世間，不應道理。
items.en: Further, what do you actually intend: is this sovereign lord included within the world, or excluded from it? If included, then this lord is no different from any other worldly phenomenon — yet claiming it alone can universally give rise to the entire world makes no sense. If excluded, then this lord must already be liberated — yet claiming a liberated being still produces the defiled, conditioned world makes no sense either.

items.title: Two More Dilemmas Close the Case Against a Creator

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？為有用故變生世間？為無用耶？若有用者，則於彼用無有自在，而於世間有自在者，不應道理。若無用者，無有所須，而生世間，不應道理。
items.en: Further, what do you actually intend: does the lord transform and produce the world because it has some use for doing so, or without any use at all? If it has a use, then it lacks mastery even over that very use — yet claiming it has mastery over the world makes no sense. If it has no use at all, then producing the world with no need or purpose whatsoever likewise makes no sense.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？此所出生，為唯大自在為因？為亦取餘為因耶？若唯大自在為因者，是則若時有大自在，是時則有出生；若時有出生，是時則有大自在；而言出生用大自在為因者，不應道理。
items.en: Further, what do you actually intend: is the world's production caused solely by the sovereign lord, or are other factors also its cause? If solely by the lord, then wherever the lord exists, the world's production must exist, and wherever production exists, the lord must exist — the two would have to be permanently co-present, making it senseless to still speak of the lord as the world's cause, as though one produced the other.

items.zh: 若言亦取餘為因者，此唯取樂欲為因？為除樂欲更取餘為因？若唯取樂欲為因者，此樂欲為唯取大自在為因？為亦取餘為因耶？若唯取大自在為因者，若時有大自在，是時則有樂欲；若時有樂欲，是時則有大自在；便應無始常有出生，此亦不應道理。若言亦取餘為因者，此因不可得故，不應道理。又於彼欲無有自在，而言於世間物有自在者，不應道理。
items.en: If other factors are also its cause, is desire alone that further factor, or something else besides desire? If desire alone, then is this desire itself caused solely by the sovereign lord, or by something else as well? If solely by the lord, then wherever the lord exists desire must exist, and wherever desire exists the lord must exist — meaning production would have to be beginninglessly, constantly ongoing, which plainly contradicts experience. And, further, if the lord itself lacks mastery over its own desire, then claiming it has mastery over the things of the world makes no sense at all.

items.zh: 如是由功用故，攝不攝故，有用無用故，為因性故，皆不應理。是故此論非如理說。
items.en: Thus, because of effort, because of what is included and what is not, because of having a function or not, and because of being a cause, none of it accords with reason. Therefore this doctrine is not soundly reasoned.

items.title: The Eighth Doctrine: Ritual Killing as the True Dharma — A Doctrine Born of Appetite, Not Reasoning

items.zh: 害為正法論者，謂如有一，若沙門、若婆羅門，起如是見，立如是論：若於彼祠中，呪術為先，害諸生命，若能祀者、若所害者、若諸助伴，如是一切皆得生天。
items.en: The doctrine that harming is the true Dharma: there are certain renunciants or brahmins who hold such a view and establish such a doctrine — that in a ritual sacrifice, once mantras are first recited, harming living beings causes everyone involved — the one who performs the sacrifice, the one who is killed, and every assistant alike — to be reborn in heaven.

items.zh: 問：何因緣故，彼諸外道起如是見，立如是論？答：
items.en: Question: For what reason do those non-Buddhist teachers hold this view and establish this doctrine? Answer:

items.zh: 此違理論，諂誑所起，不由觀察道理建立。然於諍競惡劫起時，諸婆羅門違越古昔婆羅門法，為欲食肉，妄起此計。
items.en: This doctrine, contrary to reason, arises from flattery and deceit — it is not established by any genuine examination of how things actually are. Rather, when the degenerate age of contention and strife arose, certain brahmins, departing from the ancient brahmanical teaching, fabricated this claim purely out of a desire to eat meat.

items.title: Five Dilemmas Expose the Sacrificial Mantra as Empty

items.zh: 汝何所欲？此呪術方為是法自體？為是非法自體？若是法自體者，離彼殺生，不能感得自所愛果，而能轉彼非法以為正法，不應道理。若是非法自體者，自是不愛果法，而能轉捨餘不愛果法者，不應道理。
items.en: What do you actually intend: is the mantra itself, in its own nature, wholesome, or unwholesome? If wholesome, then it should produce its own desirable result without needing killing at all — yet claiming it can transform the unwholesome act of killing into the true Dharma makes no sense. If unwholesome, then it is itself something that produces an undesirable result — so claiming it can transform other undesirable results into desirable ones makes no sense either.

items.zh: 如是記已，復有救言：如世間毒，呪術所攝，不能為害。當知此呪術方亦復如是。今應問彼：汝何所欲？如呪術方能息外毒。亦能息內貪瞋癡毒？為不爾耶？若能息者，無處無時，無有一人貪瞋癡等靜息可得，故不中理。若不能息者，汝先所說，如呪術方能息外毒，亦能息除非法業者，不應道理。
items.en: Their reply: just as worldly poison, when countered by a mantra, loses its power to harm, so too does this sacrificial mantra. One should press them: does a mantra that can neutralise external poison also neutralise the internal poisons of craving, hatred, and delusion, or does it not? If it does, then nowhere, at no time, has even a single person's craving, hatred, and delusion ever actually been neutralised this way — this plainly contradicts experience. If it does not, then your own claim — that a mantra able to neutralise external poison can likewise neutralise an unwholesome deed — makes no sense.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？此呪術方為遍行耶？不遍行耶？若遍行者，自所愛親不先用祠，不應道理。若不遍者，此呪功能便非決定，不應道理。
items.en: Further, what do you actually intend: does this mantra's effect apply universally, or not? If universally, then your failure to sacrifice your own beloved family members first makes no sense. If not universally, then this mantra's power is simply unreliable — which makes no sense for a technique claimed to guarantee heaven.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？此呪功能，為唯能轉因？亦轉果耶？若唯轉因者，於果無能，不應道理。若亦轉果者，應如轉變即令羊等成可愛妙色，然捨羊等身已，方取天身，不應道理。
items.en: Further, what do you actually intend: can this mantra's power transform the cause alone, or does it also transform the result? If the cause alone, then it has no power over the actual result — which makes no sense for something claimed to guarantee that result. If it also transforms the result, then the sacrificial animal should visibly transform into a beautiful, heavenly form on the spot — yet it must first be killed and its body discarded before any heavenly body is supposedly obtained, which makes no sense.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？造呪術者，為有力能及悲愍不？若言有者，離殺彼命，不能將彼往生天上，不應道理。若言無者，彼所造呪能有所辦，不應道理。
items.en: Further, what do you actually intend: does the one who composed this mantra possess genuine power and compassion, or not? If so, then his being unable to send beings to heaven without first killing them makes no sense — genuine power and compassion should accomplish this without any killing at all. If not, then claiming his mantra can nonetheless accomplish sending the slain to heaven makes no sense either.

items.zh: 如是由因故，譬喻故，不決定故，於果無能故，呪術者故，不應道理。是故此論非如理說。
items.en: Thus, because of the reason given, because of the example, because of indeterminacy, because of having no power over the result, and because of the one who performs the mantra, it does not accord with reason. Therefore this doctrine is not soundly reasoned.

blocks.text: Today's reading refutes the creator doctrine and then a doctrine that the treatise treats with unusual sharpness: that killing in a ritual sacrifice is religious duty. Notice the difference in tone. The earlier doctrines arose from meditation or reasoning gone wrong; this one, the treatise says, arose "from flattery and deceit".
Missing from Ru-Yi's translation, now supplied in our own: summary sentences (0309c10, 0310a14) and formal questions (0309c16, 0309c20).
A summary verse names them: function, inclusion or exclusion, usefulness, and being the cause.

items: **Function.** Does the lord's power to create arise from effort and method? If so, and nothing else in the world needs such causes, that is incoherent. Venerable Miào Jìng: "only the lord's power has effort and method as its cause; that's not fair."
**Inclusion.** Is the lord included in the world? Then it is like any worldly thing, yet produces the whole world. Excluded? Then it is liberated, yet produces the world.

**Use.** Does the lord create for some purpose? Then it lacks mastery over that purpose. Venerable Miào Jìng: "Seek nothing and you stand tall; if you seek something you must bow." Without purpose, creation is pointless.

**Cause.** If the lord alone causes everything, then whenever the lord exists, everything should exist. Venerable Miào Jìng: "In ancient times there were no aeroplanes; now there are. Was the lord's power lacking then?"

blocks.text: The underlying point is the one from Day 36: a permanent being cannot be a cause, since causes must change.

The eighth doctrine: in a sacrifice, once mantras are recited, killing a living being sends the sacrificer, the victim, and all the helpers to heaven. The treatise says this view, "contrary to reason, arises from flattery and deceit; it is not established by any genuine examination". In the degenerate age, it says, brahmins departed from the ancient teaching and invented this "purely out of a desire to eat meat". Venerable Miào Jìng agrees, bluntly: "They just wanted to eat meat."
Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Pīxún jì*, defines **deceit** (誑): "the mind full of schemes while outwardly showing another face". A religious justification for appetite is the example.

Is the mantra wholesome or not? If wholesome, it should produce good results without killing. If unwholesome, it adds bad results. Can it neutralise bad karma as mantras neutralise snake venom? Then can it neutralise the inner poisons of greed, hatred, and delusion? Venerable Miào Jìng: only the foundations of mindfulness, the eightfold path, and the holy life remove those.

Does it work universally? Then, Master Cháng Bǎi asks, why not sacrifice one's own beloved family first, to send them to heaven? Does it transform the victim? Then the animal should turn into a god on the spot, without needing to be killed.
The arguments are sharp, almost mocking, and that is deliberate. When a doctrine licenses harm, the treatise does not treat it as an honest mistake.

quiz.q: According to the summary verse, what are the four dilemmas against the sovereign maker?
options: function, inclusion or exclusion, use or uselessness, being the cause
quiz.why: "Function has no substance; inclusion and exclusion both contradict; usefulness and uselessness; and as cause, every option fails." Master Cháng Bǎi: "function has no substance" means the lord's creative power fails whether caused or uncaused.

quiz.q: The inclusion dilemma: what fault follows if the lord is included in, or excluded from, the world?
options: if included, it's like any worldly thing, yet produces the whole world; if excluded, it's liberated, yet produces the world
quiz.why: "If included, then this lord is no different from any other worldly phenomenon — yet claiming it alone can universally give rise to the entire world makes no sense. If excluded, then this lord must already be liberated — yet claiming a liberated being still produces the defiled, conditioned world makes no sense either." Master Cháng Bǎi: outside the world means liberated and uncontaminated; Venerable Miào Jìng: a liberated creator should produce only pure, peaceful dharmas.

quiz.q: The cause dilemma: if the lord is the sole cause, production exists whenever the lord does. What modern example does Venerable Miào Jìng use?
options: there were no airplanes in ancient times but now there are — if the lord is ever-present, was his power lacking then?
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The lord exists from the beginning, always; so the world should always exist too"; "in ancient times there were no airplanes, now there are — so your lord's power must have been insufficient then." Master Cháng Bǎi: cause and effect must match, yet worldly things arise and cease — contrary to perception.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what does the doctrine that harming is the true Dharma claim?
options: in a sacrifice, after reciting mantras, killing beings sends the sacrificer, the victim, and all assistants to heaven
quiz.why: "In a ritual sacrifice, once mantras are first recited, harming living beings causes everyone involved — the one who performs the sacrifice, the one who is killed, and every assistant alike — to be reborn in heaven." Master Cháng Bǎi: chant first, then kill a sheep or pig. Venerable Miào Jìng: 祠 is a place for worshipping the gods.

quiz.q: The text says in the degenerate age brahmins departed from ancient teaching and fabricated this. What do the teachers say the real motive was?
options: to eat meat — mutton, horsemeat, whatever
quiz.why: "Fabricated this claim purely out of a desire to eat meat." Venerable Miào Jìng: "They just wanted to eat meat — mutton, horsemeat, whatever"; brahmins of that age "were no longer honest or virtuous." Master Cháng Bǎi: they abandoned the earliest brahmanical law.

quiz.q: The first dilemma asks whether the mantra is itself wholesome or unwholesome. What's wrong with each answer?
options: if wholesome, it should yield good results without killing, so transforming killing into Dharma makes no sense; if unwholesome, it itself yields bad results, so it can't turn others' bad results into good
quiz.why: "If wholesome, then it should produce its own desirable result without needing killing at all — yet claiming it can transform the unwholesome act of killing into the true Dharma makes no sense. If unwholesome, then it is itself something that produces an undesirable result — so claiming it can transform other undesirable results into desirable ones makes no sense either." Master Cháng Bǎi: "dharma" here means wholesome. Venerable Miào Jìng: a good mantra would bring good results without killing.

quiz.q: The universality dilemma: if the mantra works universally, why does that fail?
options: if universal, why not sacrifice one's own beloved family first?
quiz.why: "If universally, then your failure to sacrifice your own beloved family members first makes no sense. If not universally, then this mantra's power is simply unreliable." Master Cháng Bǎi: "Why not first sacrifice the people you love and are close to?" Venerable Miào Jìng: you wouldn't like the same act done to those you love.
